text: dsh-plugin-local-infer 是面向 Web 客户端的本地推理管理插件。它把引擎服务、引擎适配器和设置卡片接入 DSH，可配置 NInfer、Hyper-Qwen、llama.cpp、Infernix、Strata 与 Basalt 等引擎。用户能查看显存估算和硬件提示，管理依赖、获取引擎、启动或停止服务，并将可用引擎登记为 DSH 模型。适合希望在自己的机器上部署和管理模型的人；运行需要相应引擎及主机依赖，无需插件 API 密钥。

dsh-plugin-local-infer manages local inference in DSH Web. Configure engines and models, estimate VRAM, review hardware guidance, launch or stop engines, and register a working engine as a DSH model. Requires the chosen engine and host dependencies; no plugin API key is needed.
想在 DSH 里配置并运行本机的大语言模型
有没有工具能估算本地模型会占多少显存
我想比较不同推理引擎的硬件适配情况
让 DSH 帮我下载并启动本地推理服务
怎样把已经启动的本地模型添加成 DSH 模型
希望在一个界面里管理引擎依赖和启动状态
I want to run a language model on my own GPU through DSH.
Can DSH estimate whether a model will fit in my available VRAM?
dsh-plugin-local-infer 的功能「显存估算」：根据模型、参数和硬件配置估算权重、KV cache 等显存占用，并给出可用预算与适配判断。 在 DSH Web 插件设置界面操作。
dsh-plugin-local-infer 的功能「引擎设置与硬件提示」：在 Web 设置卡片选择引擎和模型、调整参数，并查看硬件指导和配置状态。 在 DSH Web 插件设置界面操作。
dsh-plugin-local-infer 的功能「引擎获取与生命周期」：从设置界面管理依赖、获取引擎构建资源，并启动、停止和检查本地推理服务。 在 DSH Web 插件设置界面操作。
dsh-plugin-local-infer 的功能「登记为 DSH 模型」：将确认可用的引擎配置登记到 DSH 模型服务，也可移除已登记项。 在 DSH Web 插件设置界面操作。
dsh-plugin-local-infer 的功能「本地推理引擎适配」：注册六种引擎适配器，并加入对应预设与依赖计划。 在 DSH Web 插件设置界面操作。
dsh-plugin-local-infer 的 Orchestrator 组件在 bundle 中默认禁用；启用后才注入可编辑的系统提示词。

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that manages local inference engines:

- llama.cpp
- NInfer
- Hyper-Qwen (vLLM)
- Infernix
- Strata
- ...with more coming soon.

dsh-plugin-local-infer README · dsh-plugin-local-infer：Pick a model and an engine, tune the parameters, watch a live **VRAM Est.** meter, see **hardware warnings** the moment a value (or a parameter itself) is unsafe for the detected hardware, then the plugin manages **build, deploy, and health-check** for each engine and **automatically register it as a DSH model** once it is confirmed working. No hand-editing of finicky yaml or launchers.

dsh-plugin-local-infer README · Install：Command line:

```bash

dsh-plugin-local-infer README · Latest NPM package.：dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-local-infer
```

```bash

dsh-plugin-local-infer README · From source.：dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/cybtachyon/dsh-plugin-local-infer
```

When installing from a local checkout, run `pnpm build` first: it type-checks
the workspace (`tsc -b`) and then produces the `dsh/client.js` browser card
artifact with esbuild (`node scripts/build-client.mjs`).

Web UI: click **Plugins** → **Add Plugin** → paste `dsh-plugin-local-infer`.

Or add from the DSH Plugin Marketplace.
dsh-plugin-local-infer README · Using the plugin：The **Engine settings** card mounts on the Plugins page (older hosts: the Settings page).

dsh-plugin-local-infer README · Using the plugin：- **Pick an engine and model**, then tune the parameters. Each field renders by its type: checkboxes, dropdowns, sliders, text, directory pickers, and a chat-template combo (known templates plus free text).
- **Watch the VRAM Est. meter.** It prices weights, KV cache, overhead, and workspace against your card as you adjust values, and shows the verdict (`fits` / `tight` / `over`) and the largest context that fits.
- **Read the warnings.** Red banners and inline field warnings fire when a parameter value, or the presence of a parameter, is unsafe for your detected hardware.
- **Satisfy the system dependencies.** The panel lists each missing host dependency (docker, CUDA toolkit, ffmpeg, hf CLI, ...) with its purpose, a copy/paste install string for your OS, and an optional one-click **Run** (sudo). The **Get** button stays disabled until every dependency reports satisfied.
- **Get.** With the dependencies satisfied, `Get` syncs the engine's source: it clones the engine's git repo (or the **Engine Fork** you provided) into the **Engine Directory** override, or with no override into the engine default checkout home `~/.cache/dsh/infer/<

dsh-plugin-local-infer README · Using the plugin：When a parameter can be set both as a CLI argument and as a write to the engine's config file, the plugin prefers the CLI argument. The CLI arg is consumed for that launch only, so it leaves the on-disk config file (and any customization you made by hand in it) untouched where possible.

All values persist to `~/.dsh/local-infer/config.json`; the browser never sees a value it did not store.

dsh-plugin-local-infer README · Using the plugin：A **Get** or **Launch** that must run `sudo` first checks whether sudo credentials are cached. When they are not, both Launch buttons read **Sudo needed** (painted as a warning) and the line `Check your CLI for a sudo prompt` appears in the **Logs** section and the run's log file: the password prompt lands on the terminal that launched the harness, not in the browser. Type the password there. Without one within 60 seconds the run is killed and fails through the normal error path, and the buttons switch to **Logs**.

dsh-plugin-local-infer README · Orchestrator package：Local models often struggle with agentic workflows and can't "one-shot" prompts without assistance. The included **Orchestrator** package gives your model a default prompt that enables that capability.

dsh-plugin-local-infer README · Orchestrator package：- **Enable it** on the DeepSeek Harness **Plugins** page: open this plugin's entry and flip the **Orchestrator** component toggle (the component ships disabled). After first enabling the component, restart the host so it loads.
- **Edit the prompt** on the **Orchestrator** card that then appears: change the **Orchestrator Prompt** field and press **Save**. The default text ships in the plugin's `prompt.md`; clear the field and save to restore it.
- **It injects while enabled.** With the component enabled, the saved prompt is part of the agent's system prompt for new requests. A Save reaches the next request; no restart is needed after Save.
dsh-plugin-local-infer README · Orchestrator package：The saved prompt persists to `~/.dsh/local-infer/orchestrator.json`, beside the engine config.

dsh-plugin-local-infer README · Operating systems：| OS                           | State     | Notes                                                                                                               |
|------------------------------|-----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Linux (Debian/Ubuntu, `apt`) | Supported | Install blocks mirror the working NInfer launcher: the CUDA keyring sequence plus the compile toolchain.            |
| Linux (Arch, `pacman`)       | Supported | `pacman` blocks plus the `/opt/cuda` export lines.                                                                  |
| Linux (Fedora, `dnf`)        | Untested  | Command set present, flagged untested on a live host.                                                               |
| macOS (`brew`)               | Partial   | CPU/docker path (llama.cpp). No NVIDIA Container Toolkit on macOS, so the CUDA engines' docker path is unavailable. |
| Windows (WSL2)               | Untested  | WSL2 is detected and the dflash2 pin-memory rule fires; the command set is flagged untested.                        |
| Windows

dsh-plugin-local-infer README · Engines：| Engine            | Docker        | Local build        | State                                                                        |
|-------------------|---------------|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| NInfer            | Yes           | Yes (cmake + CUDA) | The reference engine. Measured VRAM models for the Qwen 27B/35B artifacts.   |
| Hyper-Qwen (vLLM) | Yes (compose) | No                 | `.env`-driven docker-compose profiles.                                       |
| vLLM              | No            | No                 | Work-in-progress.                                                            |
| llama.cpp         | Yes           | Yes                | Specified, not verified until the binary is available.                       |
| Infernix          | No            | Yes (cmake + CUDA) | C++/CUDA fork of NInfer tuned for Qwen models on a single RTX 50-series GPU. Local build only. |
| Strata            | Yes           | No                 | Placeholder engine; its parameter surface is empty until the flag set lands. |
dsh-plugin-local-infer README · Engines：Runtime requirements: Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`, pnpm 12.11.2 (pinned by `mise.toml`), and the `@deepseek-ai/cordis >= 4.0.6-alpha.2` peer dependency.

dsh-plugin-local-infer README · Hardware guide：What each common machine gets you in practice. Capability impressions are sourced from [r/LocalLLaMA](https://www.reddit.com/r/LocalLLaMA/) user threads. "Shared" means unified memory (the model and the OS share the pool).

dsh-plugin-local-infer README · Hardware guide：| Hardware                        | Memory          | What you get                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| NVIDIA RTX 5090                 | 32 GB VRAM      | Reliably fits model weights up to 23 GB with 240k+ context and vision. Handles complex coding and vision tasks, but needs special tooling for very long or complex tasks.     |
| NVIDIA RTX 4090                 | 24 GB VRAM      | The community workhorse. 30B-class models fit at Q4 and drive coding agents; 70B needs slow CPU offload. Best speed-per-dollar single card.                                   |
| NVIDIA RTX 3090                 | 24 GB VRAM      | The used-card value king. Same 24 GB as a 4090 but an older generation: 32B at Q4 with modest context, no FP8. A single card is limiting; the common advice is to pair two.   |
| N
